newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia talks tough on NATO ahead of talks.
newsitem.headline: Russia talks tough on NATO ahead of talks.

text.p: Russia took a tough line against NATO eastward expansion plans on Tuesday, one day before talks in Brussels between Foreign Minister Yevgeny Primakov and alliance foreign ministers.

"Russia's position on this issue remains firm and rather tough," President Boris Yeltsin's press secretary, Sergei Yastrzhembsky told a Kremlin briefing. "It is a step which would lead only to negative consequences."
"Our position is well known, it has not changed," said Yastrzhembsky. He said there had been some new ideas coming from the West which would be discussed at the Brussels meeting.
Western leaders have repeatedly said accession talks will start for some former communist-ruled states in Eastern and Central Europe next year, whatever Moscow's objections.

Russia says such enlargement would threaten its security. Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin reiterated those fears at a European security summit in Lisbon last week, but most other leaders backed NATO's plans.
Primakov is due to leave Moscow later on Tuesday. He is expected to meet NATO Secretary-General Javier Solana before flying home on Thursday.
